Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:10:1.hebrew: והא "וכן" קתני - דמשמע תרוייהו חד טעמא הוא, גינה וחצר:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:10:1.english: But it teaches "and similarly" - For it implies that both have one and the same reason, [namely] a garden and a courtyard.

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:11:1.hebrew: מחייבין אותו - והכא לא קתני "רצו", אלא על כרחו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:11:1.english: They compel him - And here it does not teach "they wanted," but rather [that he is compelled] against his will.

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:11:2.hebrew: נפל שאני - שכבר נתרצו הראשונים בכותל:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:11:2.english: [A wall that] fell is different - For the first [partners] already consented to the wall.

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:12:1.hebrew: ודקארי לה מאי קארי לה - וכי לא ידע דנפל שאני:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:12:1.english: And as for [the one] who objected to it, what was he objecting to? - Did he not know that [the case of a wall that] fell is different?

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:12:2.hebrew: סיפא איצטריך ליה - כלומר, הוא הדין נמי מעיקרא. והאי דקתני "נפל" משום סיפא, לאשמועינן דיותר מד' אמות אין מחייבין, ואע"פ שהראשון היה גבוה יותר, לא מחייבין ליה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:12:2.english: He needed it for the latter clause - That is to say, the same law applies from the outset as well. And the reason it teaches "fell" is because of the latter clause, to teach us that for more than four cubits we do not obligate [him], and even though the first [wall] was taller, we do not obligate him.

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:13:1.hebrew: כופין אותו - כל אחד מבני החצר לתת חלקו בבנין:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:13:1.english: We compel him - Each one of the residents of the courtyard [is compelled] to contribute his share toward the construction.

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:13:2.hebrew: בית השער - שבונים כותל נגד השער עגול סביב, ועושין באותו היקף פתח קטן מן הצד, משום היזק ראיות בני רה"ר, שלא יראו תוך החצר:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:13:2.english: The gatehouse - That they build a round wall opposite the gate, all around, and they make a small opening in that enclosure on the side, because of the damage of sight [caused by] the people of the public domain, so that they will not see into the courtyard.

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:13:3.hebrew: הזיקא דרבים - שכל בני רה"ר מסתכלין שם:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:13:3.english: The damage of the public - For all the people of the public domain look in there.

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:14:1.hebrew: אין חולקין - אין האחד כופה את חבירו לחלוק:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:14:1.english: We do not divide - One [partner] cannot compel his fellow to divide [the courtyard].

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:15:1.hebrew: החלונות - אחד מבני השותפין הבונה כותל בחצר כנגד חלונותיו של חבירו, בין מלמעלה וכו' — אם הכותל גבוה יותר מן החלונות, צריך להגביה למעלה מהן ד"א, כדמפרש ואזיל, כדי שלא יסמוך על כותלו וישחה ויראה בחלונותיו של חבירו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:15:1.english: The windows - One of the partners who builds a wall in the courtyard opposite the windows of his fellow, "whether above, etc." — if the wall is higher than the windows, he must raise it four cubits above them, as [the Gemara] explains as it proceeds, so that [a person] will not lean on his wall, bend down, and see into his fellow's windows.

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:15:2.hebrew: בין מלמטה - אם הכותל נמוך מן החלונות, צריך להשפילו מהן ד"א, כדי שלא יעמוד על עובי כותלו ויראה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:15:2.english: Whether from below - If the wall is lower than the windows, one must lower it [i.e., the wall] four cubits from them [the windows], so that [a person] will not stand on the thickness of his wall and look [into the neighbor's property].

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:15:3.english: And opposite them - One must distance the wall from the windows by four cubits, so that it will not darken [them].

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:16:1.english: The damage of a house is different - For a person does private things in his house.

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:17:1.hebrew: מעקה גבוה ארבע אמות - כדי שלא יראה בחצר חבירו כשהוא משתמש בגגו:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:17:1.english: A parapet four cubits high - So that he will not see into his neighbor's courtyard when he uses his roof.

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:17:2.english: And I do not know at what time you come - to make use of your roof.

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:1:1.hebrew: קידש - התבואה, אם הוסיף מאתים. לישנא דקרא נקט: "פן תוקדש" (דברים כב):
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:1:1.english: It has become consecrated - The grain, if he added [a crop worth] two hundred [zuz]. He used the language of the verse: "lest it be forfeited as consecrated" (Deuteronomy 22).

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:2:1.hebrew: וטעמא דרצו - לבנות כותל, דמדעת שניהן הוא דחייביה חכמים שיבנו בין שניהן. ולקמן פריך: כשרצו מאי הוי? ליהדרי בהו! אבל לא רצו שניהן, שהיה אחד אומר: דייה לחלקה במסיפס של יתדות עצים תקועים בארץ נמוכים — לא כייפינן ליה, ואין זה יכול לומר לו: איני חפץ שתראה עסקי:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:2:1.english: And the reason is that they wanted - to build a wall; for it is only by the consent of both of them that the Sages obligated them to build [a wall] between the two of them. And later [the Gemara] asks: If they wanted, what of it? Let them retract! But if both did not want [a wall] — for example, where one said, "It is enough to divide his portion with a fence of wooden stakes fixed low in the ground" — we do not compel him, and the other cannot say to him, "I do not want you to see my affairs."

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:3:1.hebrew: פלוגתא - חלוקת חצר שהושוו דעתם לחולקה, וכגון שלא היה בה ח' אמות כדי לזה וכדי לזה, שאין האחד יכול לכוף את חבירו לחולקה. ולהכי תני "שרצו", שכיון שרצו לחולקה, בונין כותל אבנים על כרחם. ואם בא האחד לומר: אי איפשי ביציאה זו, אלא מסיפס בעלמא — אין שומעין לו, משום היזק הראיה:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:3:1.english: A dispute - [This refers to] dividing a courtyard, where they agreed to divide it, for example where it did not have eight cubits, enough for this one and for that one, so that one cannot compel his fellow to divide it. And therefore [the Mishnah] teaches "that they wanted," because once they wanted to divide it, they build a stone wall [even] against their [individual] will. And if one of them comes and says, "I do not want this expense, but only a mere partition (*mesips*)," we do not listen to him, because of the damage of being seen (*hezek re'iyah*).

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:4:1.hebrew: הוה אמינא במסיפס בעלמא - מיירי מתני', דאיהו נמי מחיצה איקרו. ורצו דקתני, אחלוקה קאי, וכשאין בה דין חלוקה. קמ"ל כותל. ורצו דקתני משום כותל, דאי לא רצו פלגי לה במסיפס:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:4:1.english: I would have thought [that it refers] to a mere mesifas - The Mishnah is speaking [of this], for it too is called a "partition." And [the word] "they wished" that it teaches refers to the division, [even] when [the courtyard] is not subject to the law of division. [Therefore] it teaches us [about] a wall. And [the word] "they wished" that it teaches is on account of the wall, for if they did not wish [to build a wall], they divide it with a mesifas.

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:6:1.english: That one of them persuaded his fellow - He asked him to divide it with a partition.

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:6:2.hebrew: מהו דתימא א"ל כשנתרציתי לך - במחיצה, מחיצה דקה נתרציתי, ולמעוטי באוירא, כגון של נסרים, שהיא דקה והיזק ראיה אין בה. או תמשוך עובי הכותל בחלקך, חוץ מדבר מועט. אבל לבנות כותל אבנים עב, למעוטי נמי תשמישתי, לא נתרציתי:
Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:6:2.english: What might you have said? [That] he said to him, "When I agreed to you" - [I agreed] to a partition; I agreed to a thin partition, and to diminish [my share] in the airspace, such as one of planks, which is thin and has no [concern of] damage of sight. Or [that] you would extend the thickness of the wall into your own portion, except for a small amount. But to build a thick stone wall, which would also diminish my usage, I did not agree.

Rashi on Bava Batra 2b:9:1.english: It is forbidden for a person to stand, etc. - So that he does not harm it with an evil eye.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:11:1.hebrew: נפל שאני - שהורגלו לעשות דבר הצנע בחצר, ולא למדו ליזהר זה מזה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:11:1.english: A fallen [wall] is different - For [the residents] were accustomed to do private matters in the courtyard, and they did not learn to guard themselves against one another [seeing them].

Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:12:1.hebrew: ודקארי לה מאי קארי לה - כלומר: פשיטא דנפל שאני, ואדרבה היה לו להוכיח מדקתני "ונפל" מכלל דבעלמא לא שמיה היזק:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:12:1.english: "And as for the one who raised [the objection], what was he raising?" - That is: It is obvious that [the case of a wall that has] fallen is different; and on the contrary, he should have proven [his point] from the fact that [the Mishnah] teaches "and it fell," which implies that in other cases it is not called damage.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:13:1.hebrew: הזיקא דרבים שאני - ואע"ג דלקמן משמע דאיירי בחצר שאינה סמוכה לרה"ר, מ"מ איכא היזקא דרבים, דזימנין דדחקי רבים ועיילי להתם, כדאמרי' לקמן. ורשב"ג, אע"ג דלית ליה האי טעמא דזימנין דדחקי רבים, מ"מ מרחוק יכולין לראות לפנים, ולכך לא פליג אלא אבית שער; אבל בדלת מודה דכופין אותו לבנות:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:13:1.english: The damage [caused by exposure] to the public is different - Even though later [in the Gemara] it implies that [the Baraita] is speaking of a courtyard that is not adjacent to the public domain, nevertheless there is damage [caused by exposure] to the public, for sometimes the public is crowded and they enter there, as we say later. And [as for] Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, even though he does not hold this reason that sometimes the public is crowded, nevertheless [people] can see inside from a distance, and therefore he disagrees only regarding a gatehouse; but regarding a door, he agrees that we compel him to build [one].

Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:14:1.hebrew: מאי לאו בכותל - תימה, ויהא בכותל? דילמא הכי פי': אין חולקין את החצר, אפי' האחד רוצה לבנות את הכותל בתוך שלו, עד שיהא בה ד' אמות לכל אחד; הא אם יש בה ד' אמות לכל אחד — חולקין, אם רצה לכנוס ולבנות בתוך שלו. וי"ל דחולקין משמע באמצע, דאי אשמועינן כדפי', הוה ליה למיתני: אין עושין כותל בחצר עד שיהא כו':
Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:14:1.english: "What, does this not [refer] to a wall?" - It is puzzling: [granted that it is about a wall,] so let it be about a wall! Perhaps it means this: We do not divide the courtyard, even if one [partner] wants to build the wall within his own [portion], unless it has four cubits for each one; but if it has four cubits for each one, they do divide it, if he wishes to withdraw and build within his own [portion]. And one can answer: The word "divide" implies [building the wall] in the middle; for if [the Baraita] were teaching us as I explained, it should have taught: "We do not make a wall in a courtyard unless it has, etc."

Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:17:1.hebrew: שאני התם דאמר ליה בעל החצר לבעל הגג כו' - תימה: אמאי לא מייתי מדתניא לקמן (בבא בתרא דף ו:): "שתי חצירות זו למעלה מזו, לא יאמר העליון: הריני בונה מכנגדי ועולה, אלא מסייע מלמטה ובונה"; אלמא שמיה היזק:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:17:1.english: "It is different there, since the owner of the courtyard said to the owner of the roof, etc." - It is puzzling: Why does [the Gemara] not bring proof from what was taught later (Bava Batra 6b): "[With] two courtyards, one higher than the other, the upper one may not say: 'I will build [the wall] opposite my [level] and go up,' but rather he assists from below and builds"? Evidently, [seeing into another's property] is called damage (hezek).

Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:1:1.hebrew: נתיאש הימנה ולא גדרה - דוקא נתיאש; אבל לא נתיאש ועוסק כל שעה לגדור, אע"פ שהוסיף מאתים — מותר. כדתנן במסכת כלאים (פ"ה מ"ו): הרואה ירק בכרם ואמר: "כשאגיע לשם אלקטנו", הוסיף מאתים — מותר; "לכשאחזור אלקטנו", הוסיף מאתים — אסור. אלמא כשהוא מחזר אחר לקיטתו, אפילו הוסיף מאתים — מותר. והטעם יש לפרש משום דכתיב (דברים כ״ב:ט׳): "לא תזרע כרמך כלאים" — דומיא דזריעה דניחא ליה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:1:1.english: If he despaired of it and did not fence it - Specifically [where] he despaired; but if he did not despair and is engaged at every moment in fencing it, even if [the crop] grew by a two-hundredth, it is permitted. As we learned in tractate Kilayim (5:6): One who sees a vegetable [growing] in a vineyard and says, "When I reach there I will pick it," and [in the meantime] it grew by a two-hundredth — it is permitted; [if he says,] "When I return I will pick it," and it grew by a two-hundredth — it is forbidden. Evidently, when he is actively seeking to pick it, even if it grew by a two-hundredth, it is permitted. And the reason should be explained as being because it is written (Deuteronomy 22:9): "You shall not sow your vineyard with diverse kinds" — [the prohibition applies only to a case] similar to sowing, [where the planting] is something he desires.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:1:2.hebrew: וחייב באחריותו - אע"ג דהיזק שאינו ניכר לא שמיה היזק (גיטין נג.), נראה לר"י דהאי חשיב היזק ניכר, שהרי ניכר הוא שהוא כלאים כשרואה הגפנים בשדה. ומטמא, אע"פ שרואין השרץ על הטהרות, לא חשיב היזק ניכר, דמי יודע אם הוכשרו? אבל אין לומר דה"נ הוי היזק שאינו ניכר, וקנסוהו כמו במטמא (שם), שלא יהא כל אחד הולך ומטמא טהרותיו של חבירו; דהכא ליכא למיחש להכי, שבעל הכרם נמי מפסיד. ועוד, אי קנס הוא, במזיד דוקא היה לו להתחייב:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:1:2.english: "And he is liable for its responsibility" - Although unseen damage is not considered damage (Gittin 53a), it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak that this counts as visible damage, for it is evident that [the field] is kilayim when one sees the vines in the field. But [in the case of] one who renders [something] impure, even though one sees the creeping creature on the pure foods, it is not considered visible damage, for who knows whether they had been made susceptible [to impurity]? But one cannot say that here too it is unseen damage, and they penalized him as in the case of one who renders [food] impure (ibid.), so that each person should not go and render his fellow's pure foods impure; for here there is no need to worry about this, since the owner of the vineyard also loses out. And furthermore, if it were a penalty, he should have been liable only in the case of an intentional act.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:3:1.hebrew: ואימא מאי מחיצה פלוגתא - מפרש ר"י: משום דעל לשון גודא יש כמה קושיות, כדפריך בסמוך, לפיכך דוחק לפרש מחיצה פלוגתא, אע"ג דבכל מקום הוי מחיצה גודא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:3:1.english: "And say that mechitza means a dispute" - Ri explains: Since there are several difficulties with the term guda ["wall"], as [the Gemara] asks shortly afterward, it is therefore forced to explain mechitza as [meaning] a dispute, even though everywhere else mechitza means a wall (guda).

Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:3:2.hebrew: וכיון דרצו בונין את הכותל בעל כרחו - לקמן מוקי לה כשאין בה דין חלוקה. ותימה לר"י: דאמאי נקט תנא דמתני' באין בה דין חלוקה, וקתני רצו? לא ליתני רצו, ולאיירי בשיש בה דין חלוקה! ותי': דקמ"ל, דס"ד בשאין בה דין חלוקה דמצי למימר: כי איתרצאי לך לחלוק ע"מ שלא לעשות גודא, אבל על מנת לעשות גודא לא איתרצי לך. ויש ספרים דמקשין, ומתרץ כן להדיא בשילהי שמעתין:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:3:2.english: "And since they agreed, they build the wall against his will" - Below (the Gemara) establishes it [as referring to a case] where [the courtyard] is not subject to the law of division. And Rabbenu Yitzchak was puzzled: Why did the Tanna of our Mishnah choose [a case] where it is not subject to the law of division, and yet teach "they agreed"? Let him not teach "they agreed," and let him speak of a case where it is subject to the law of division! And he answered: [The Mishnah] is teaching us [this], for one might have thought, in a case where it is not subject to the law of division, that [the partner] could say: "I agreed with you to divide on the condition that we not make a wall, but on the condition of making a wall, I did not agree with you." And there are books [i.e., texts] that pose [this as] a question and answer it so explicitly at the end of this discussion.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:4:1.hebrew: הוה אמינא במסיפס בעלמא - פי': "ורצו" דקתני אמסיפס. ואע"ג דבלאו רצו נמי עושין מסיפס בעל כרחם, כדמוכח בסמוך דקאמר: "מאי לאו בכותל? לא, במסיפס" — היינו מסיפס גרוע; אבל כי רצו, עושין מסיפס מגויל וגזית כמנהג המדינה, ומקרי מסיפס לפי שהוא מלא חלונות, כדפי' בערוך, ואינו מגין מהיזק ראיה. א"נ, לפי שאינו גבוה י', כדמוכח לקמן גבי גג הסמוך לחצר, דאמר ר"נ: עושה לו מעקה גבוה י'. ופריך: למאי? אי להיזק ראיה — ד"א בעינן, ואי לנתפס כגנב — במסיפס סגי. ובקונטרס פי' דרצו דקתני אחלוקה קאי, ותימה: דהא אסיק דמחיצה היינו גודא, דאי פלוגתא — לחצות מיבעי ליה. ועוד, היכי מצי למימר דה"א במסיפס בעלמא? הא שמעינן ליה מסיפא דקתני: "אבל בזמן ששניהם רוצים אפילו פחות מכאן יחלוקו", והיינו לכל הפחות במסיפס. ועוד, היכא המ"ל במסיפס בעלמא? הא בהדיא קתני במתני' גזית וגויל:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:4:1.english: "I would have thought [it refers] to a mere lattice" - Explanation: The word "they wish" that the Mishnah teaches refers to the lattice. And even though, without their wishing, they also make a lattice against their will, as is evident shortly afterward where it says, "What, is it not [referring] to a wall? No, [it refers] to a lattice" — that is, an inferior lattice; but when they wish, they make a lattice of rough stones and hewn stones, according to the custom of the locality. And it is called a lattice because it is full of windows, as I explained in the Arukh, and it does not protect against the damage of being seen. Alternatively, [it is called a lattice] because it is not ten [handbreadths] high, as is evident below regarding a roof adjacent to a courtyard, where Rav Nachman said: He makes himself a parapet ten [handbreadths] high. And [the Gemara] asks: For what purpose? If for the damage of being seen — we require four cubits; and if [it is] so that he not be caught like a thief — a lattice suffices. And in the Kuntres [Rashi] he explained that "they wish" that the Mishnah teaches refers to the division, but this is surprising: for the Gemara concluded that "partition" means a wall, since if [the Mishnah meant] a dispute, it should have said "to divide." Moreover, how could it say "I would have thought, a mere lattice"? We already learn it from the latter clause, which teaches: "But when both of them wish, even less than this, they may divide," and that means at the very least with a lattice. Moreover, how could one say [that it refers to] a mere lattice, when the Mishnah explicitly teaches "hewn stones and rough stones"?

Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:5:1.hebrew: בונין את הכותל באמצע פשיטא - למ"ד גודא — פריך, כמו כל הנך פירכי דלקמן, דכשהקנו לעשות גודא, כך הקנה זה כמו זה, ופשיטא דבאמצע. אבל למ"ד פלוגתא — איצטריך למימר: סד"א דמשום היזק ראיה יש לו לסייע בבנין הכותל, אבל אין לו לבנות בחלקו בשביל כך:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:5:1.english: "They build the wall in the middle" – this is obvious! - According to the one who says [that the dispute concerns] a guda (a wall), [the Gemara's question] is a valid challenge, like all those challenges below: for when they ceded [rights] to make a wall, this one ceded just as much as that one, and it is obvious that [it is built] in the middle. But according to the one who says [that the dispute concerns] a peluganta (a division), it was necessary to state [this]: One might have thought that because of the damage of seeing, he is obligated to help in building the wall, but he need not build [it] on his own portion for that reason.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:8:1.hebrew: תא שמע וכן בגינה - לקמן מסקינן דה"ק: וכן בגינה סתם, כמקום שנהגו לגדור דמי. הלכך דייק שפיר דהיזק ראיה שמיה היזק:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:8:1.english: Come and hear: "And so too with a garden" - Later (3a) we conclude that this is what it means to say: "And so too with a garden," without specification, is like a place where they are accustomed to build a wall. Therefore, [the Gemara] inferred correctly that damage from being seen is considered damage:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:9:1.hebrew: גינה שאני כדרבי אבא וכו' - וא"ת: ומהאי טעמא יתחייב נמי לגדור בבקעה? ויש לומר: דשאני גינה, שמגדלין בה ירק לאכילה, וכל שעה היא עומדת בקמותיה. אבל בקעה אינה עומדת בקמותיה אלא חדש אחד בשנה, ולא מיחייב לגדור; אבל אסור לעמוד בשעה שעומדת בקמותיה. וא"ת: ולמ"ד פלוגתא, כיון דאשמועינן דאפילו בחצר שמיה היזק, כל שכן בגינה! ואמאי איצטריך תו למיתני "וכן בגינה"? וי"ל: דאיצטריך "וכן בגינה" למיתני משום גויל וגזית:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 2b:9:1.english: A garden is different, in accordance with Rabbi Abba, etc. - And if you ask: By this reasoning, should one also be obligated to build a fence in a valley? And one can say: A garden is different, because vegetables for eating are grown in it, and at every moment it is standing in its crops. But a valley stands in its crops only one month of the year, and [therefore] one is not obligated to fence it; however, it is forbidden to stand [in a neighbor's field] at the time when it is standing in its crops. And if you ask: According to the one who says that [the Mishnah's ruling] is a dispute [i.e., that the partition is by agreement only], since [the Mishnah] already teaches us that even in a courtyard [looking in] is called damage, all the more so in a garden! So why was it necessary again to teach, "and likewise in a garden"? And one can say: It was necessary to teach "and likewise in a garden" because of [the ruling about] rough stones (gevil) and hewn stones (gazit).
